newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mostly firmer.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mostly firmer.

text.p: Dec 10 - IMM currency futures ended quiet, orderly trade mostly firmer. One bank, thought to represent a fund, sold about 5,000 Dec/March Swiss franc spreads. Rolling otherwise far slower than on Monday. Sterling gained notably on yen on talk of Eurotunnel-related buying. Resistance held, more downside seen in marks, yen, Swiss soon.
Monday's cleared volume totalled 63,119 mark, 61,303 yen, 49,078 Swiss franc, 40,250 sterling, and 19,178 Canadian dollar futures contracts.
Price boards just before Tuesday's close showed estimated combined December and March volume of 33,000, 19,800 and 31,000 in yen, marks and Swiss francs, respectively.
One bank, thought to represent a large fund, sold about 5,000 December/March Swiss franc spreads Tuesday, but brokers said spread volume otherwise was far lower than Monday.
Intermarket spread activity appeared thin even though spot sterling racked up gains notably against yen.
"The largest intermarket spread showing (on the price boards) is a 40-lot," added the broker.
"That just shows what goes through the pits," added another floor broker. "It doesn't mean some guy didn't do 10,000 (spreads) by legging them."

Sterling advanced partly on talk of Eurotunnel-related buying by Japanese banks. Yen drew some buying against dollars on cash-market talk that Japanese Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo) is set to begin hedging its foreign bond holdings with currency forwards, although futures brokers said they heard little about the Kampo rumors on the floor.

Futures briefly worked upward again after the U.S. October wholesale inventories rose 0.6 percent and September was revised upward, while the third quarter U.S. current account gap widened to a record $47.96 billion.
But nearby marks and Swiss francs backed down again from resistance near the morning's peaks and also failed to extend ranges on the downside, technicians said.

March yen ended flat at $0.008939, marks rose $0.0017 to $0.6477, Swiss francs rose $0.0009 to $0.7609, sterling rose $0.0042 to $1.6488, Can dollar lost $0.0020 to $0.7408, Aussie dollar fell $0.0028 to $0.7996, peso rose $0.000575 to $0.120650.
